question: If $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, find $(2\vec{b})\times(3\vec{a})$.
explanation:
Step 1: Scalar factors can be taken outside a vector product, so $(2\vec{b})\times(3\vec{a})=6(\vec{b}\times\vec{a})$.
Step 2: The vector product is anti-commutative, giving $\vec{b}\times\vec{a}=-(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})$.
Step 3: Therefore, $(2\vec{b})\times(3\vec{a})=-6(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})$.
Step 4: Substitute $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$.
Step 5: Multiplication gives $-12\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-18\hat{k}$.
Final Answer: $(2\vec{b})\times(3\vec{a})=-12\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-18\hat{k}$.
